title: Customer feedback notes — Auto-rollback on SLO breach (latency/error) [working]
body:
Context / why I’m collecting this
- We keep hearing some version of: “rollouts break latency and we only notice after customers complain.” The ask is consistent across Dedicated + enterprise Hosted: automatically revert traffic when SLO breaches, but do it in a way that doesn’t create churn/flapping.
- These notes are intentionally raw. I’m capturing exact phrasing where possible + translating into requirements.

How to read this doc
- “Customer” names are anonymized (or use segment label).
- I’m grouping by: (1) reliability pain, (2) policy semantics, (3) visibility/audit, (4) control/override, (5) safe-guards.
- At the end: prioritized requirements + proposed default policy knobs (candidate defaults, not final).

---

Customer snippets (anonymized)

1) Enterprise Hosted (regulated SaaS, NA) — from support escalation (SUP-18421) + follow-up email (Gmail thread)
- “We cannot be the canary for your model changes. If latency blows up we need it to revert without a human having to notice.”
- “If rollback happens, we need a clear record of what changed and why. Our incident reviews require attribution.”
- “Our big concern is blast radius. If you roll back everyone at once, it could cause another incident.”
- “We want guardrails around low-traffic routes; we’ve seen false alarms when traffic is tiny.”
- “Per-region matters. EU west was fine, US east was not. Rolling back globally would be wrong.”

Translated requirements
- Auto-rollback must support per-tenant / per-route / per-region evaluation (or at least per-region rollback action) to avoid global overreaction.
- Provide audit trail including: policy definition at the time, monitor values used, and who/what triggered the action.
- Provide rate-limits / dampening to prevent cascading rollbacks (esp. correlated infra events).

2) Dedicated customer (mid-market fintech) — from FF tech deep dive (ff-90113)
- “We already have SLOs and paging; what we don’t have is something that actually flips traffic back.”
- “We’re okay with aggressive rollback as long as it’s deterministic and we can tune it.”
- “Don’t page us for every canary bump. If you can roll back automatically, page only if rollback fails or if it keeps happening.”
- “Make sure you can tell the difference between ‘bad rollout’ vs ‘monitor is down.’ If monitoring is down, don’t do random rollbacks.”

Translated requirements
- Separate: (a) decisioning, (b) execution. Different alert policies.
- “Unknown” health state needs explicit handling; customers want predictable behavior in monitor outage cases.
- Expose tunable parameters + sane defaults.

3) AI-native startup (high volume, hosted) — informal feedback relayed by CS (no ticket)
- “Our rollout windows are short; if it doesn’t roll back within minutes, it’s not helpful.”
- “We need a warm-up grace period. Every deployment causes a brief spike and it’s normal.”
- “Can you compare against baseline rather than some static threshold? We use different models per route; absolute numbers vary.”

Translated requirements
- Fast detection windows with minimum traffic constraints.
- Warm-up/grace period required.
- Baseline comparison is strongly desired (must-be-worse-than-baseline / delta-based guardrail).

4) Enterprise Dedicated prospect (HubSpot 49244) — change management heavy
- “Auto-rollback is good, but we need approvals/controls: who can enable it, who can disable it, who can acknowledge the event.”
- “We need separate policies per environment: staging vs prod. And separate for canary vs full rollout.”
- “We need an API we can query for current verdict; our NOC wants to display it.”

Translated requirements
- RBAC + audit on policy changes + manual override/ack.
- Environment-scoped configuration.
- Console/API surface for verdict + history.

5) Customer reporting “unexpected rollbacks” (SUP-18457)
- “We saw rollback triggered, but the route had only a handful of requests.”
- “The monitor graph in the dashboard looked stale; it’s unclear what the controller read.”
- “If this rolls back too often, we’ll just turn it off.”

Translated requirements
- Minimum traffic gating and/or “min requests per window.”
- Monitor staleness checks + explicit “data unavailable” handling.
- Rollback flapping prevention and transparency (show exactly what inputs triggered rollback).

6) Dedicated + multi-region enterprise (SUP-18490)
- “We need different thresholds by region and by tier.”
- “Dedicated cluster is predictable; Hosted burst behavior is different. Don’t use one-size-fits-all thresholds.”

Translated requirements
- Policy overrides by region and capacity tier.
- Tiered SLO definitions and policy templates.

---

Common themes (what customers repeatedly ask for)

A) Predictability > sophistication
- Customers are okay with simple rules (fixed threshold + cooldown) if they are consistent, visible, and tunable.

B) Guardrails against flapping / noise
- Warm-up grace period (deploy + cache warm-up)
- Minimum traffic thresholds
- Cooldown period after rollback / after a breach
- Baseline comparisons to avoid triggering on normal variance

C) Visibility and auditability
- “Show me the verdict, show me why, show me what you did.”
- They want “evidence” attached: monitor values, window, baseline, and the policy parameters.

D) Control and governance
- RBAC for enabling/disabling policy, editing thresholds
- Manual override (pause auto-rollback for an incident / planned experiment)
- Acknowledgement flow (so oncall can mark “known issue” and suppress repeats)

E) Region and tenancy specificity
- Rollback should not necessarily be global; route+region granularity is a consistent request.
- Enterprise customers want per-tenant customization (at least as an add-on / advanced config).

---

Requirements list (prioritized)

P0 (must-have for v1)
1) Cooldown + warm-up/grace support
- Customers view this as essential to avoid disabling feature after a few false positives.
- Warm-up should be explicit and visible (“evaluation paused until X”).

2) Minimum traffic gating
- Example gating: min requests per window, min tokens per window (tokens might be better for LLM endpoints), or both.
- If under min traffic: verdict should be “insufficient_data” not “healthy.”

3) Audit + history for actions
- Record: policy at the time, monitor identity, query template version, decision trace, executor action details.
- Must be viewable in console and exportable via audit logs.

4) “Unknown” / monitor outage handling
- Must distinguish: “breach” vs “no signal.”
- Customers strongly prefer not to auto-rollback on missing data.

5) Per-route and per-region evaluation
- Even if config is templated, execution should be capable of scoping (route+region).

P1 (important; customers asked, but can be phased)
6) Baseline comparison (“must be worse than baseline”)
- Helps with heterogeneous routes/models.
- Prefer: compare canary vs stable or current vs last known good (depending on rollout type).

7) Per-tenant overrides
- Enterprise expects ability to tune thresholds (at least for Dedicated).
- Could be via policy overrides or per-tenant policy objects.

8) Notification controls
- Customers want fewer pages if auto-rollback succeeded.
- Page if: rollback failed, repeated rollbacks, or big impact.

P2 (nice-to-have / future)
9) Advanced multi-window/burn-rate semantics
- A few SRE-savvy customers asked about burn rate; most just want something understandable.

10) Customer-facing API for verdict + history
- Some enterprise NOCs want this; might be satisfied by console + event webhooks.

---

Policy defaults (candidate; to review with SRE + control plane)

Goal: defaults that avoid false positives but still roll back within ~5–10 minutes on real regressions.

Suggested default knobs (v1)
- Evaluation window: 5 minutes (rolling)
- Evaluation cadence: 1 minute
- Warm-up grace after starting canary: 10 minutes (configurable; might vary by model size)
- Minimum traffic: 200 requests per window OR 2M tokens per window (TBD which is more robust)
- Latency SLO signal: p95 (or p99?) over window; initial preference from customers is p95 for stability; SRE might prefer p99 for tail.
- Error SLO signal: 5xx rate over window (exclude 4xx; confirm treatment of 429s)
- Cooldown after rollback: 30 minutes (no further automatic rollbacks for that route/region)
- Cooldown after breach without rollback (if action blocked by gating): 10 minutes
- Monitor staleness threshold: if last datapoint > 3 minutes old => verdict “unknown”

Notes to self
- Minimum traffic should be based on the exact metric used for SLO (request count that matches monitor query). Otherwise mismatches create confusion.
- Warm-up should not hide real issues for too long. Consider a two-phase warm-up: first N minutes only evaluate errors, not latency.

---

UX / Console implications (from customer expectations)

What customers want to see in the UI
- Current verdict: healthy / breaching / insufficient_data / unknown
- “Why” details: metric, window, threshold, baseline (if used)
- Timeline: when breach started, when rollback decision made, when traffic changed, when stable recovered
- Manual controls: pause policy, disable policy, acknowledge breach, and link to runbook

Audit log expectations
- “Automated rollback triggered” event needs: route, region, tenant, rollout id, from_version -> to_version, policy id/version, decision inputs.
- “Policy changed” needs: who changed, diff summary, reason (free text), ticket link.

---

Open questions (to resolve with Eng/SRE)
1) Per-tenant overrides: do we want “policy per tenant” in v1 schema, or only templates by tier/route/region?
2) Baseline definition: compare against last stable version’s SLO, against pre-rollout window, or against stable cohort in same time window?
3) Fail-open vs fail-closed: customer preference is generally “don’t rollback on unknown,” but SRE may want fail-closed for high-risk tiers.
4) How do we prevent correlated incidents from causing widespread rollbacks?
- Options: global rate limiting, require baseline comparison, or require multiple regions to confirm (careful: that might slow reaction).

---

Next steps
- Align P0 list with Marissa (PRD) and Rafael/Miles (runbook + paging policy).
- Ask Allison to sanity-check default windows/metrics and how we present ‘unknown’ vs ‘insufficient_data’.
- Follow up with SUP-18457 customer after we define min-traffic + staleness safeguards (they are at risk of churn if we ship without this).

Scratchpad / extra quotes (not cleaned up)
- “If you roll back, don’t make us guess which model build was bad.”
- “We need to justify changes to auditors; auto-actions without logs are a non-starter.”
- “We care about p95 not p50. Tail is what breaks our app.”
- “Please don’t rollback because of one-minute blips.”
